newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Philips cuts more non-core units.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Philips cuts more non-core units.

text.p: Dutch giant Philips Electronics NV said Friday it planned to shed small underperforming businesses, including one New Jersey-based business, to free up resources to expand core activities.
In a brief statement, Philips said its Industrial Electronics (IE) division would sell nine small operating companies this year, adding to a string of minor sell-offs by the group in recent months.
"Philips (IE)...announced its intention to further stimulate growth in several of its operating companies," the group said.
"This decision, which will allow the division to focus on and strengthen its key businesses, will also lead to nine smaller operating companies being sold."
It said the companies concerned employ about 1,500 staff and made up about 15 percent of total Industrial Electronics sales.

The firms to be sold off are: Edax International of Mahwah, N.J.; Philips Power Systems of Wavre, Belgium; Thermocoax of Suresnes, France; Philips TV Test Equipment of Brondby, Denmark; Philips Weighing and Philips Electronic Centre of Hamburg, Germany; Philips Industrial Automation Systems of Eindhoven and PBF of Almelo in the Netherlands; and Philips Kistaindustrier AB of Kista, Sweden.

Philips' IE division will now focus on several clusters of activities, such as analytical equipment, communication and security products and systems, electronic production equipment and industrial and infrastructure projects, it said.
